title: Build a Multi-Layer Perceptron From Scratch
description: Construct a complete feedforward neural network from mathematical primitives in pure Python, including matrix forward passes, cross-entropy loss, and backpropagation.
problemStatement: As an aspiring AI research engineer, you must demonstrate fundamental mathematical mastery of neural networks before using high-level frameworks. Your objective is to build a complete 2-layer neural network from scratch using only Python and NumPy (no PyTorch, TensorFlow, or Scikit-Learn). Your network must learn the non-linear XOR boundary or spiral dataset, iteratively updating weights using analytical backpropagation.
requirements: Initialize weights using He/Kaiming initialization to avoid symmetry and saturation.
Implement a vectorized forward pass supporting input matrices X of shape (batch_size, n_features).
Implement non-linear ReLU activation for hidden layers and Sigmoid/Softmax for output.
Compute Binary Cross-Entropy loss between predicted probabilities and target labels.
Implement analytical backward propagation computing exact partial derivatives (dL/dW2, dL/db2, dL/dW1, dL/db1) using the chain rule.
Execute gradient descent updates: W := W - alpha * dL/dW over 500+ training epochs.
Achieve >= 98% accuracy on the non-linear classification dataset.
hints: Remember that the derivative of ReLU(z) is 1.0 where z > 0 and 0.0 where z <= 0.
The derivative of Binary Cross-Entropy combined with Sigmoid output simplifies cleanly to (y_hat - y).
Keep learning rate around 0.1 to 0.5 for small scratch networks.
expectedOutput: Console logging showing loss decreasing per 100 epochs (e.g. Epoch 100: Loss 0.42 -> Epoch 500: Loss 0.03) and final test accuracy exceeding 98%.
